facts.statement: The genus Yunnanosaurus was first described by C. C. Young in 1942.
facts.quote: authority: Young, 1942

facts.statement: This large, ground-dwelling quadrupedal herbivore could also walk on two legs and measured up to 7 meters long and 2 meters high.
facts.quote: Yunnanosaurus was a large sized, moderately-built, ground-dwelling, quadrupedal herbivore, that could also walk bipedally, and ranged in size from 7 meters (23 feet) long and 2 m (6.5 ft) high to 4 m (13 ft) high in the largest species.

facts.statement: The first skeletons were discovered by Yang Zhongjian in the Sinemurian stage of the Early Jurassic.
facts.quote: Yang Zhongjian (also known as C. C. Young) discovered the first Yunnanosaurus skeletons in the upper Zhangjiawa Member of the Lufeng Formation of Yunnan, China, dating to the Sinemurian stage of the Early Jurassic.

facts.statement: The original discovery included over twenty incomplete skeletons and two skulls excavated by Tsun Yi Wang.
facts.quote: The fossil find was composed of over twenty incomplete skeletons, including two skulls, it was excavated by Tsun Yi Wang.

facts.statement: A new species, Y. youngi, was described in 2007 by Lü Junchang and colleagues.
facts.quote: In 2007, Lü Junchang and colleagues described another species of Yunnanosaurus, Y. youngi (named in honor of C. C. Young).

facts.statement: The species Y. youngi reached a length of 13 meters, making it significantly larger than Y. huangi.
facts.quote: In addition to various skeletal differences, at 13 meters (42 ft) long Y. youngi was significantly larger than Y. huangi (which reached only 7 meters [23 ft]).

facts.statement: A juvenile individual assigned to Y. robustus was described in 2013 by Sekiya et al.
facts.quote: In 2013, Sekiya et al. described the discovery of a juvenile individual which was assigned to Yunnanosaurus robustus.

facts.statement: A juvenile Y. robustus shows tooth-tooth wear facets and coarse serrations, suggesting a unique feeding mechanism.
facts.quote: This individual possesses characteristic dentition that suggests a potentially unique feeding mechanism as evidenced a tooth–tooth wear facet on its mesial maxillary and dentary teeth, and maxillary teeth that have coarse serrations.

facts.statement: Yunnanosaurus had over sixty spoon-shaped teeth that were self-sharpening by wearing against each other during feeding.
facts.quote: There were more than sixty spoon-shaped teeth in the jaws of Yunnanosaurus, and were unique among early sauropodomorphs in that its teeth were self-sharpening because they "[wore] against each other as the animal fed."

facts.statement: Sekiya et al. (2013) differentiated Y. robustus from Y. huangi by describing a juvenile specimen.
facts.quote: However, Sekiya et al. (2013) described a juvenile of Y. robustus and were able to differentiate it from Y. huangi.

facts.statement: Recent analyses place Yunnanosaurus in the taxon Massopoda within a clade including Anchisaurus and Jingshanosaurus.
facts.quote: a more recent phylogenetic analysis conducted by Novas et al. (2011) shows that this genus is part of the taxon Massopoda in a clade with Anchisaurus and Jingshanosaurus.

facts.statement: The skull of Y. huangi is distinguished by features such as a small external naris, a robust nasal process, and narrow maxillary teeth without denticles.
facts.quote: According to Barrett et al. (2007), the skull of Y. huangi can be distinguished from other sauropodomorphs based on the following characteristics: a small external naris a robust expanded nasal process of the premaxilla a downward projection from the rear of the maxillary ascending process no nutritive foramina on the lateral surface of maxilla a shallow circular depression on the lateral surface of the ventral lacrimal process a midline boss near the front of the frontals a prominent midline boss on the parietals the anterolateral process of the parietal is expanded relative to the width of the posterolateral process the maxillary teeth are narrow and do not have denticles

facts.statement: Y. youngi is distinguished from Y. huangi by having the longest sixth cervical vertebra and tightly fused sacral vertebrae.
facts.quote: According to Lu et al. (2007), Y. youngi can be distinguished from Y. huangi based on the following characteristics: the sixth cervical vertebra is the longest among the vertebral column the neural spines of the posterior cervical vertebrae are short with an expanded distal end, which is wider than its anteroposterior length three sacral vertebrae are tightly fused with a stout sacrocostal yoke the ventral margin of the postacetabular process of the ilium is slightly concave the ischium is longer than the pubis the distal end of the pubis is round

facts.statement: Y. robustus is distinguished by the absence of anteroposterior expansion on the astragalus and a dorsoventrally compressed metatarsal IV shaft.
facts.quote: According to Sekiya et al. (2013), Yunnanosaurus robustus can be distinguished from other sauropodomorphs based on the following characteristics: the absence of the anteroposterior expansion on the medial end of the astragalus the shaft of the metatarsal IV is dorsoventrally compressed

facts.statement: Dental microwear analysis indicates Yunnanosaurus fed on less tough and fibrous plants than later sauropods.
facts.quote: According to dental microwear texture analysis (DMTA), Yunnanosaurus fed on plant material that was much less tough and fibrous than the plants later sauropods like Omeisaurus, Camarasaurus, and Euhelopus fed on.

facts.statement: Type specimens of Y. huangi and Y. robustus were found in the Huangchiatien locality of the Lufeng Formation in Yunnan.
facts.quote: The type specimens of Yunnanosaurus huangi and Yunnanosaurus robustus were recovered in the Huangchiatien (Dahungtien) locality of the Lufeng Formation in Yunnan, China.

facts.statement: Specimens of Y. huangi and Y. robustus are housed at the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology in Beijing.
facts.quote: These specimens are all housed in the collection of the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology, in Beijing, China.

facts.statement: Yunnanosaurus shared its environment with ornithischians, other sauropodomorphs, and theropods like Sinosaurus and Eshanosaurus.
facts.quote: Yunnanosaurus huangi and Yunnanosaurus robustus shared their paleoenvironment with the ornithischians Bienosaurus, and Tatisaurus, the sauropodomorphs Gyposaurus, Lufengosaurus, and Jingshanosaurus, and the theropods Sinosaurus triassicus and Eshanosaurus.

facts.statement: Yunnanosaurus was a quadrupedal sauropodomorph that could also stand upright on its hind legs.
facts.quote: Yunnanosaurus fue un sauropodomorfo que se desplazaba en cuatro patas pero podía erguirse sobre sus patas traseras.

facts.statement: Yunnanosaurus possessed more than sixty spoon-shaped teeth in its jaws.
facts.quote: Había más de sesenta dientes en forma de cuchara en las mandíbulas de Yunnanosaurus

facts.statement: Its teeth were unique among early sauropodomorphs because they self-sharpened by wearing against each other while the animal ate.
facts.quote: eran únicos entre los primeros sauropodomorfos en que sus dientes se autoafilaban porque "se desgastaban unos contra otros mientras el animal se alimentaba".

facts.statement: The species showed a large size difference, with Y. youngi reaching 12 meters and Y. huangi reaching 7 meters.
facts.quote: Las especies tenían gran diferencia de tamaño, 12 metros para Y. youngi contra 7 metros Y. hangi.

facts.statement: The type species Yunnanosaurus huangi was described in 1942 by Yang Zhongjian, known as C.C. Young in the West.
facts.quote: La especie tipo fue descrita en 1942 con el nombre de Yunnanosaurus huangi por Yang Zhongjian, conocido como C.C. Young en Occidente por aquel entonces.

facts.statement: A second species, Yunnanosaurus robustus, was described in 1951, and a third, Yunnanosaurus youngi, was named in 2007.
facts.quote: En 1951 describió una segunda especie, Yunnanosaurus robustus, y en 2007, Lu et al., nombraron a la tercera especie Yunnanosaurus youngi.

facts.statement: They lived in the early Jurassic period, between 199 and 183 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivieron a principios del período Jurásico, hace desde 199 a 183 millones de años, desde el Sinemuriense al Pliensbachiense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: Fossils were found in Yunnan province, China, within sediments of the Lufeng Formation.
facts.quote: Sus Fósiles fueron encontrados en la provincia China de Yunnan, en sedimentos de la Formación Lufeng.

facts.statement: C.C. Young discovered the first Yunnanosaurus skeletons in the upper member of Zhangjiawa, Lufeng Formation, Yunnan, China, dating to the Sinemurian stage of the early Jurassic.
facts.quote: Yang Zhongjian, conocido como C. C. Young en occidente, descubrió los primeros esqueletos de Yunnanosaurus en el miembro superior de Zhangjiawa de la Formación Lufeng de Yunnan, China, que data de la etapa Sinemurense del Jurásico temprano.

facts.statement: The fossil bed contained more than 20 incomplete skeletons, including two skulls, which were excavated by Tsun Yi Wang.
facts.quote: El lecho fósil encontrado estaba compuesto por más de 20 esqueletos incompletos, incluidos dos cráneos, fue excavado por Tsun Yi Wang.

facts.statement: The holotype of Y. youngi was collected in 2000 from terrestrial sediments deposited during the Pliensbachian stage of the early Jurassic, approximately 191 to 183 million years ago.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo de Y. youngi se recolectó en el año 2000 en sedimentos terrestres depositados durante la etapa Pliensbachiense del período Jurásico temprano, hace aproximadamente 191 a 183 millones de años.

facts.statement: Yunnanosaurus was previously assigned to various taxa including Thecodontosauridae and Plateosauridae.
facts.quote: Yunnanosaurus había sido asignado a varios taxones a lo largo de los años, incluidos Thecodontosauridae y Plateosauridae

facts.statement: A 2011 phylogenetic analysis by Novas et al. showed that Yunnanosaurus belongs to the taxon Massopoda in a clade with Anchisaurus and Jingshanosaurus.
facts.quote: un análisis filogenético más reciente realizado por Novas et al. de 2011 muestra que este género es parte del taxón Massopoda en un clado con Anchisaurus y Jingshanosaurus.

facts.statement: The parent group of Yunnanosaurus is Sauropodiformes.
facts.quote: Parent group: Sauropodiformes

facts.statement: Researchers do not consider Yunnanosaurus to be especially close to sauropods in phylogeny because the rest of the animal's body has a clearly "prosauropod" design.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, los investigadores no consideran que Yunnanosaurus esté especialmente cerca de los saurópodos en filogenia porque las partes restantes del cuerpo del animal tienen un diseño claramente "prosaurópodo".

facts.statement: Similarities in tooth shape are not evidence of close phylogenetic relationship but rather an example of evolutionary convergence.
facts.quote: Dichas similitudes no son pruebas de una cercanía filogenética entre los géneros, sino que más bien son un ejemplo de convergencia evolutiva.

facts.statement: Specimen ZMNH-M8739 consists of partial cranial material and an almost complete postcranial skeleton.
facts.quote: El espécimen ZMNH-M8739 consta de material craneal parcial y un esqueleto poscraneal casi completo.

facts.statement: This individual possesses characteristic dentition suggesting a potentially unique feeding mechanism, demonstrated by tooth-to-tooth wear facets on mesial maxillary and dentary teeth, and maxillary teeth with coarse serrations.
facts.quote: Este individuo posee una dentición característica que sugiere un mecanismo de alimentación potencialmente único, como lo demuestra una faceta de desgaste diente a diente en sus dientes mesiales maxilares y dentarios, y dientes maxilares que tienen aserraduras gruesas.
